bihar.title: Holi being played in a courtyard
bihar.creator: Unknown Patna artist
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page licence template {{PD-Art|PD-old-100-expired}}; source British Library Online Gallery Add.Or.939. Painted c. 1795 by an anonymous artist, so the work is far out of copyright.
bihar.shows: A long whitewashed hall with a blue-and-white striped floor. A crowd of men and women in white jamas and saris dance with raised arms, a woman squirts coloured water from a long brass pichkari, drummers play a red dhol and a frame drum (daf), a woman bends over a pot of colour, and a patron sits on a stool at left with a sitar player. Fresh guests arrive through a curtained doorway at right.
zoom_details: woman squirting colour from a long pichkari, centre-left (~40% x, 70% y)
drummers with a red dhol and a raised daf, left of centre (~27% x, 68% y)
seated host and sitar player beside a patterned pillar, far left (~10% x, 75% y)
guests arriving through the curtained doorway, far right (~93% x, 72% y)
bihar.why: A Patna painting of Phagua/Holi: colour, drums and dancing in one room. It reads as a Bihari family celebration and carries the haldi mood of colour thrown at people, or the sangeet mood of drums and dance.
bihar.concerns: Very wide (2.2:1) with a large empty wall above the crowd, so the pinned frame needs a crop to the lower half. Pale palette. British Library itself does not offer a CC licence; this rests on PD-Art (old 2D work), which the brief accepts.

bihar.title: Durga Puja
bihar.creator: Sewak (Sevak) Ram (c. 1770 to c. 1830)
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page {{PD-Art|PD-old-100}}; author Sevak Ram died c. 1830; source British Library Add.Or.29.
bihar.shows: A pillared hall with three arches and glass wall lamps. Singers in white raise their arms in song, a drummer beats a large barrel drum and a boy plays cymbals; a patron with a hookah sits at left. At right stands a painted clay image of Durga on her lion with Lakshmi, Saraswati, Ganesha and Kartikeya on his peacock, under a red arch of painted panels, with plates of offerings on stands before her.
zoom_details: singers with arms raised mid-song, centre-left (~35% x, 60% y)
drummer and cymbal player seated on the floor, centre (~50% x, 68% y)
Ganesha at Durga's feet beside the lion, lower right (~78% x, 70% y)
the painted arch (chalchitra) and Durga's face, upper right (~85% x, 35% y)
bihar.why: By the best-known Patna Kalam painter. Music and song before the goddess suits the sangeet; the Ganesha at the goddess's feet could open the invocation in a Bihari, rather than Rajasthani, picture.
bihar.concerns: Durga Puja is more Bengali than Bihari, though this was painted in Patna. Lots of plain wall in the upper half. PD-Art via Commons; British Library offers no CC licence of its own.

bihar.title: Mailah-Jahn (a mela; apparently a Ram Lila or Dussehra fair)
bihar.medium: Graphite, watercolour and gouache with gold on laid Indian paper, 58.1 x 41 cm
bihar.creator: Sewak Ram (c. 1770 to c. 1830), Patna
bihar.source: Museum of Fine Arts, Houston (2008.434), via Wikimedia Commons
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page {{PD-Art|PD-old-auto-1923|deathyear=1830}}, source mfah.org/art/detail/71290. A second Commons copy from Google Arts & Culture (2401x1707) records MFAH rights policy only, not a CC licence.
bihar.shows: A vast crowd in white turbans at a fair. At left, caparisoned elephants with gilded howdahs carry the patron under parasols. Centre, a float carries Rama and Sita enthroned side by side, crowned, with banana plants; men in Hanuman and monkey masks dance around it. A drummer rides a horse at right, women sit on a mound at lower right, and a giant Ravana effigy rises from a fort in the distance.
zoom_details: Rama and Sita enthroned together on the float, centre-left (~40% x, 62% y)
dancers in monkey and Hanuman masks, centre (~50% x, 70% y)
elephants with golden howdahs and parasols, left (~15% x, 55% y)
the Ravana effigy on its fort, far right (~78% x, 55% y)
bihar.why: Sita is Mithila's own princess, and Bihari wedding songs sing of every bride as Sita and every groom as Ram. A Patna painting with the divine couple enthroned at the centre of a joyful crowd suits the shaadi, or the two-homes chapter as Bihar en fete.
bihar.concerns: Upper 45% is sky, so tours stay in the lower half. MFAH has not published an open licence; this rests on PD-Art (old 2D work), which the brief accepts.

bihar.title: A wedding procession by night; a groom sitting in a palanquin, preceded by musicians, torch-bearers, guards and attendants
bihar.place: India (eastern India; probably Patna or Murshidabad, not attributed by Wellcome)
bihar.medium: Gouache with watercolour on paper, 16.8 x 23 cm
bihar.creator: Unknown Indian (Company school) artist
bihar.licence_evidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue API: digitised image location licence "pdm", credit "Wellcome Collection" (work xjsngwqj).
bihar.shows: A baraat under a starry night sky: torch-bearers with flaming tridents, a band with long trumpets, cymbals and a red dhol, porters with water pots slung on a bahangi pole, shield- and spear-bearers, then the groom wearing a tall crown seated in a red-canopied palanquin carried on poles, and a white horse led behind.
zoom_details: the crowned groom in his red palanquin, centre-right (~58% x, 72% y)
band with trumpets, cymbals and red dhol, left (~18% x, 72% y)
flaming torch tridents against the stars, upper left (~25% x, 45% y)
porter with pots on a carrying pole (bahangi), centre-left (~33% x, 78% y)
bihar.why: The groom arriving at night with music and torches is exactly the Bihari baraat, and the crown he wears is close to the Bihari maur. Dark, starry and dramatic: a strong Shaadi plate.
bihar.concerns: Wellcome gives only "India"; the eastern Company style fits Patna or Murshidabad, but the place is unproven, so label it "North India" unless the family is happy with "probably Patna".

bihar.title: People bathing and praying in the holy river Ganga (a Chhath scene)
bihar.place: India (style of Patna mica painting; not attributed by Wellcome)
bihar.creator: Unknown Indian artist
bihar.licence_evidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue API: licence "pdm", credit "Wellcome Collection" (work juq4nm6m).
bihar.shows: Women in white saris stand waist-deep in the river holding up bamboo trays (soop) heaped with bananas and sweets to the sky; a crowd of women in red, pink, yellow and blue sits on the bank behind big baskets (daura) of fruit, more arrive with baskets on their heads, and boys swim among floating flowers to collect offerings.
zoom_details: woman in the water raising a soop of bananas, centre (~40% x, 60% y)
women seated on the bank with daura baskets of fruit, upper right (~75% x, 55% y)
women arriving with baskets on their heads, top centre (~60% x, 42% y)
boys swimming among red flowers, bottom (~50% x, 88% y)
bihar.why: Wellcome calls it simply bathing in the Ganga, but the soop trays of bananas raised from the water are unmistakably Chhath, the festival that most says "Bihar". For a Bihari family this is home.
bihar.concerns: The Chhath reading is mine (strong but not the catalogue's); the place is not attributed (Patna or Benares mica style). Top 35% is blank mica. Companion Wellcome image mn94s8r5 (women selling offerings on the bank) is an alternate.

bihar.title: Eight Great Events Stele
bihar.creator: Unknown sculptor
bihar.licence_evidence: Met Collection API object 705435: isPublicDomain true; Met Open Access images are CC0.
bihar.shows: A pale stone stele: the Buddha touching the earth at Bodh Gaya under the leafy canopy of the Bodhi tree, flanked by two standing bodhisattvas; the Buddha's death (parinirvana) across the top; tiers of tiny seated and standing Buddhas for the other great events; Mara's demons tumbling at the lotus base; and friezes of elephants, lions and little narrative scenes below.
zoom_details: the Buddha's face under the Bodhi-tree canopy, centre (~50% x, 40% y)
reclining Buddha (parinirvana) along the top (~50% x, 18% y)
Mara's demons at the base of the throne, lower centre (~50% x, 68% y)
frieze of elephants and lions, bottom (~50% x, 82% y)
bihar.why: The enlightenment at Bodh Gaya, carved in Bihar: the strongest single image of Bihar's Buddhist heritage, rich in details for a tour. It links his home state with her faith.
bihar.concerns: Small object (25 cm) photographed against grey; crop the background. Similar pale steles were also made in Burma for Bodh Gaya pilgrims, but the Met says Bihar.

bihar.title: A wedding procession: the groom riding on a horse accompanied by people playing music and carrying colourful pennants
bihar.place: India (style of Patna mica painting; not attributed by Wellcome)
bihar.creator: Unknown Indian artist
bihar.licence_evidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue API: licence "pdm", credit "Wellcome Collection" (work kzcg7xuw).
bihar.shows: A packed baraat on a pink mica ground: an elephant with riders and tall red-and-green banners at left, drummers and trumpeters in white jamas and coloured sashes, then the groom in yellow with a gold crown on a prancing horse, under golden paper-flower trees, gilded fans and a hanging lantern carried on poles.
zoom_details: the crowned groom on his horse, right of centre (~73% x, 65% y)
drummers with dholak and nagara, centre-left (~32% x, 72% y)
elephant, riders and great banners, left (~15% x, 50% y)
golden flower-tree decorations and lantern, upper right (~85% x, 42% y)
bihar.why: A crowded, colourful barat with the groom on his ghodi: a Shaadi alternative to the night procession, or a Sangeet plate for the band.
bihar.concerns: Place not stated by Wellcome. The Indian Museum, Kolkata labels mica paintings in the same style "Patna, 19th century", but this one is unproven. Upper 40% is blank mica. Two near-identical Wellcome versions exist (kcbysmzc, stained; xjftjt5y, mounted) as alternates.

bihar.title: The Chowk and the main street of Patna
bihar.creator: Sita Ram, painting for Lord Moira (later Marquess of Hastings)
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page {{PD-art|PD-old-100-1923}}; source British Library Online Gallery Add.Or.4700.
bihar.shows: Patna's main bazaar street in soft light: two-storey houses with tiled shop awnings and carved balconies, two domed chhatris over gateways, a great tree at right, a porter with a carrying pole, a horseman, and a domed bullock carriage (rath) in the foreground.
zoom_details: the domed bullock carriage and horseman, bottom centre (~50% x, 82% y)
porter with baskets on a carrying pole, lower left (~25% x, 82% y)
domed chhatri pavilion over the street, centre (~45% x, 40% y)
shopfronts with tiled awnings, left (~20% x, 62% y)
bihar.why: The groom's Patna 200 years ago, by an Indian painter: a calm, beautiful city scene to set beside a Pune view in the two-homes chapter.
bihar.concerns: No people in close focus; the details are small, so zooms must be generous. PD-Art via Commons.

bihar.title: Five Cosmic Buddhas, inner top cover of a Perfection of Wisdom manuscript
bihar.place: Text copied at Vikramashila Monastery, Bihar; covers painted in Nepal
bihar.medium: Gum tempera, colours and paper on wood, 6.5 x 57 cm
bihar.creator: Unknown monastic scribes and painters
bihar.licence_evidence: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API: share_license_status "CC0" for 1938.301.b.
bihar.shows: A long red wooden board painted with five seated Buddhas in haloes (white Vairochana at centre, blue Akshobhya touching the earth, Ratnasambhava, Amitabha, Amoghasiddhi), each flanked by small attendant figures, separated by green diamond panels around the two binding holes.
zoom_details: white Vairochana at the centre (~50% x)
blue Akshobhya touching the earth, left (~20% x)
a small attendant bodhisattva, centre-left (~38% x)
green lattice panel round a binding hole, right of centre (~66% x)
bihar.why: A Buddhist blessing written in Bihar 900 years ago: a bridge from his Bihar to her Buddhism, and a natural invocation that pans across the Buddhas one by one.
bihar.concerns: Extremely wide (6.7:1): needs a horizontal pan rather than a pinned frame, or a crop. Cleveland states the paintings were made in Nepal (Kathmandu) and only the text at Vikramashila. Companion bottom cover 1938.301.189.a (four bodhisattvas round Vajrasattva) is equally fine. Full file is a TIFF; a 3400 px JPEG is at openaccess-cdn.clevelandart.org/1938.301.b/1938.301.b_print.jpg.

bihar.title: A high ranking man smoking a hookah and watching musicians and dancing girls
bihar.place: India (Patna mica style; compare the Indian Museum, Kolkata "Nutch party", labelled Patna)
bihar.creator: Unknown Indian artist
bihar.licence_evidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue API: licence "pdm", credit "Wellcome Collection" (work jj69zjdz).
bihar.shows: Under a red-poled canopy with a diamond-patterned valance, a host in a brocade coat leans on a bolster with a tall coiled hookah; two dancers in full red and green skirts twirl, singers and musicians with sarangi, tabla and a tanpura stand at right, and attendants with peacock-feather fans stand behind the host.
zoom_details: two dancers mid-twirl, centre (~60% x, 62% y)
musicians with sarangi, tabla and tanpura, right (~88% x, 58% y)
host with the coiled hookah, left (~28% x, 62% y)
peacock-feather fans held high, upper left (~18% x, 40% y)
bihar.why: A Patna-style evening of music and dance: the closest 19th-century picture of a sangeet night.
bihar.concerns: Courtesan dance (mujra/nautch) context, which some elders may not like for a family sangeet. Mica is flaking at the top edge. Place not stated by Wellcome.

bihar.title: A marriage ceremony: the bride, in red, stands on a raised platform and is hiding from the groom behind a white sheet
bihar.place: India (north or eastern India; not attributed)
bihar.creator: Unknown Indian artist
bihar.licence_evidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue API: licence "pdm", credit "Wellcome Collection" (work n4r348pf).
bihar.shows: A courtyard of a big house roofed by a huge maroon canopy, its walls hung with carpets. Dozens of women in veils sit and stand around a low red-draped platform where the bride in red waits; women hold up a white sheet between her and the groom. In the foreground: brass vessels, plates and pots (the dowry or ritual vessels), a drum and a covered basket.
zoom_details: the bride in red on the platform, centre (~58% x, 72% y)
women raising the white sheet, centre (~48% x, 68% y)
brass vessels and plates laid out, lower left (~30% x, 88% y)
women singing round a drum, lower right (~90% x, 85% y)
bihar.why: The only 19th-century picture found of the ceremony itself from the women's side: crowded, warm and full of detail.
bihar.concerns: The sheet held between bride and groom suggests the Muslim arsi-mushaf rite, so it may not read as a Hindu (or Buddhist) wedding; place unknown (Lucknow, Patna or Murshidabad style). Use only if the family is comfortable with that.

bihar.title: A group of seven female musicians seated under a canopy
bihar.creator: Shiva Lal (Patna, mid-19th century)
bihar.licence: NOT openly licensed by the V&A; underlying painting public domain (PD-Art argument only)
bihar.licence_evidence: V&A terms of use (vam.ac.uk/info/va-websites-terms-conditions): non-commercial use, digital images max 768 px, credit "(c) Victoria and Albert Museum, London". No Commons copy found.
bihar.shows: Seven women with covered heads sit close together under a red-poled canopy: one plays a dholak, another a sitar, another small kettle drums, the rest sing. A bottle, a covered brass box and a lota sit on the white floorcloth before a blue-and-white striped edge.
zoom_details: woman playing the dholak, left (~25% x, 62% y)
woman with the sitar, centre (~62% x, 60% y)
singers' faces under their veils, centre top (~45% x, 48% y)
brass box and lota on the floorcloth, bottom (~45% x, 82% y)
bihar.why: A Patna painting by Shiva Lal of women singing to the dholak: exactly the geet-gawai that is the Bihari sangeet. The best fit in this whole search for that chapter.
bihar.concerns: Licence is the problem: the V&A image is only licensed for non-commercial use at 768 px, so it fails the strict rule. Usable only if the team accepts the PD-Art position (a faithful photo of a 160-year-old painting is not itself copyrightable, as Wikimedia holds) or uploads it to Commons under PD-Art first. Only 2500 px tall. Big blank canopy and floor.

bihar.title: Golghar at Bankipur, near Patna
bihar.creator: Robert Smith (Royal Engineer, died 1873)
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page {{PD-Art|PD-old-auto-expired|deathyear=1873}}; source British Library WD 2090.
bihar.shows: The beehive-shaped Golghar granary rising over Bankipur's riverfront, with palms, bungalows and a moored ship, seen across the wide grey Ganga with a small boat in the foreground.
zoom_details: the Golghar dome and its stair, centre (~50% x, 38% y)
boat on the Ganga, lower left (~25% x, 70% y)
riverside bungalows and ship's masts, right (~75% x, 45% y)
bihar.why: Patna's best-known landmark on the river: a simple, recognisable "home" image for the groom's side.
bihar.concerns: By a British engineer, not a Bihari painter. Few details for a tour (more of a single-view plate).

bihar.title: Four women selling food-grains, vegetables and fruit
bihar.medium: Watercolour, with purple and gold-flecked borders
bihar.creator: Shiva Dayal Lal (1815 to 1884)
bihar.source: Victoria and Albert Museum (IS.66-1949), via Wikimedia Commons
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page {{PD-Art|PD-old-100}}; artist died 1884. Image originates from the V&A, whose own terms are non-commercial.
bihar.shows: Four women in saris of violet, green, pink and yellow sit behind rows of baskets of grains, lentils, spices and vegetables, with a pair of scales, stacked earthen pots and a palm tree, under a pale sky with blue hills.
zoom_details: woman in yellow with baskets of greens and gourds, right (~82% x, 55% y)
baskets of yellow and red grains and spices, lower left (~25% x, 72% y)
woman weighing on a hand balance, left (~20% x, 45% y)
stacked earthen pots, far left (~8% x, 40% y)
bihar.why: Bright, warm and full of yellow and turmeric tones, by Patna's leading mid-century painter: it can carry the haldi chapter with grains, spices and women in yellow.
bihar.concerns: Market, not a ritual. Only 2500 px wide. The Commons copy is PD-Art from a V&A photograph; the V&A itself claims non-commercial terms.

bihar.title: Eight Great Events from the Life of the Buddha
bihar.creator: Unknown sculptor
bihar.licence_evidence: AIC API artwork 130676: is_public_domain true; API licence text: data and public-domain images under CC0.
bihar.shows: A dark stone stele: the Buddha standing in the centre, his robe in fine ripples, with niches on both sides holding the other events (birth, enlightenment, first sermon, taming the elephant, descent from heaven), and the parinirvana across the top.
zoom_details: the standing Buddha's face, centre top (~50% x, 25% y)
small seated Buddha in a side niche, left (~25% x, 40% y)
parinirvana at the crown, top (~50% x, 8% y)
donor figures on the base, bottom (~50% x, 92% y)
bihar.why: Very high resolution Pala stele from Bihar; an alternative to the Met stele.
bihar.concerns: Dark stone, less contrast than the Met stele. AIC's IIIF server sits behind Cloudflare; the full size may need /full/3000,/ or downloading from the artwork page.

bihar.title: Model of the Mahabodhi Temple
bihar.creator: Unknown sculptor
bihar.licence_evidence: Met Collection API object 73214: isPublicDomain true.
bihar.shows: A small dark stone pilgrim's souvenir of the Bodh Gaya temple: the tall tiered tower covered in niches with tiny Buddhas, corner turrets, and a pillared shrine at the base.
zoom_details: the stepped tower with rows of niches, upper centre (~50% x, 30% y)
tiny seated Buddhas in niches, middle (~45% x, 55% y)
pillared entrance shrine, lower right (~65% x, 70% y)
bihar.why: A 900-year-old pilgrim's model of the Mahabodhi temple: Bodh Gaya in the hand, a quiet emblem of Bihar meeting Buddhism.
bihar.concerns: Small object on a white background; best as an emblem or seal rather than a full tour.

bihar.title: Votive plaque with figure of the Buddha, temple at Bodhgaya, and stupas
bihar.creator: Unknown
bihar.licence_evidence: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API: share_license_status "CC0" for 1985.219.
bihar.shows: A tear-shaped red clay pilgrim's plaque: the Buddha seated touching the earth inside the Mahabodhi temple's arch, small stupas on either side, the temple spire above, and the Buddhist creed in tiny script along the base.
zoom_details: the seated Buddha, centre (~50% x, 50% y)
the temple spire, top (~50% x, 12% y)
small stupas, left and right (~20% x and 80% x, 40% y)
the line of inscription, bottom (~50% x, 85% y)
bihar.why: A keepsake that pilgrims took home from Bodh Gaya 1,100 years ago, which fits a page about inviting guests.
bihar.concerns: Single-colour clay; modest detail.

bihar.title: Two women facing each other
bihar.medium: Ink and colour on paper, 25.3 x 27.1 cm
bihar.creator: Unknown Mithila woman painter
bihar.licence_evidence: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API: share_license_status "CC0" for 2005.80.
bihar.shows: Two women in saris face each other under a pink canopy held on striped painted poles, like a wedding marwa; one holds a small pot. A big four-petalled flower floats between them over a chequered ground, and the border is a ring of decorated, lidded pots.
zoom_details: the woman at left with the small pot, left (~25% x, 45% y)
striped painted canopy poles, centre (~50% x, 30% y)
the four-petalled flower between them, centre (~50% x, 48% y)
border of decorated pots, edges (~10% x, 50% y)
bihar.why: A Mithila painting of women meeting under a painted canopy, which can be read as women's wedding rites (the marwa with painted bamboo poles, ritual pots). Openly licensed Madhubani is rare.
bihar.concerns: Cleveland's title is neutral; the wedding reading is mine. Simple drawing, small sheet, so zoom levels are limited. Post-1965 work by an unnamed and possibly living artist, released CC0 by the museum (the brief accepts museum CC0).

bihar.title: Four-armed goddess, with hearts in margin
bihar.medium: Ink and colour on paper, 36.2 x 27 cm
bihar.creator: Unknown Mithila woman painter
bihar.licence_evidence: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API: share_license_status "CC0" for 2005.86.
bihar.shows: A goddess in pink and yellow with a lotus and a discus, her skirt spreading like a peacock's tail, surrounded by flowers, fish, birds and lotuses in magenta, yellow and black, inside a border of red hearts.
zoom_details: the goddess's face and lotus, upper centre (~45% x, 25% y)
peacock-tail skirt, lower centre (~50% x, 75% y)
fish and birds among the flowers, left (~15% x, 50% y)
border of hearts, edge (~50% x, 3% y)
bihar.why: The brightest and busiest of the Cleveland Mithila sheets, full of the fish, lotus and bird motifs of Maithil wedding art; colour suited to haldi.
bihar.concerns: Same CC0-by-museum basis as the other Cleveland Mithila sheets. A goddess rather than a wedding scene. The family dropped Cleveland's Mithila Ganesha (2005.84) before for not sitting with finer paintings, so it may need its own page.

bihar.title: Embroidered sari (odhni)
bihar.medium: Silk and metal thread and sequins on cotton, 197.5 x 122 cm
bihar.creator: Unknown Patna embroiderers
bihar.licence_evidence: Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API: share_license_status "CC0" for 1916.1215.
bihar.shows: A rose-pink cloth with diagonal bands of gold zardozi vines over a net of gold stitching, framed by wide silver-gilt borders and fringed ends.
zoom_details: diagonal band of gold vine embroidery, centre (~50% x, 50% y)
silver-gilt border pattern, left end (~8% x, 50% y)
sequins and net stitching on pink silk, upper centre (~40% x, 25% y)
bihar.why: A Patna bridal-looking cloth in red-pink and gold at enormous resolution: a texture or backdrop for the shaadi, matching the Paithani on the bride's side.
bihar.concerns: Worn in places; a textile, so more of a background than a tour.

bihar.title: The Harihar Kshetra festival (Sonepur Mela)
bihar.creator: Sewak Ram (c. 1770 to c. 1830)
bihar.licence: NOT openly licensed by the V&A; underlying painting public domain (PD-Art argument only)
bihar.licence_evidence: V&A terms of use: non-commercial, max 768 px online, "(c) Victoria and Albert Museum, London". No Commons copy found.
bihar.shows: The great November fair at the meeting of the Gandak and the Ganga: a sea of pilgrims pours down to the river, tents for notables in the foreground, a European couple watching, an elephant in the crowd, and the river packed with boats and budgerows under a big tree.
zoom_details: the crowd pouring to the river, lower centre (~45% x, 80% y)
boats and sailing budgerows on the river, centre (~35% x, 55% y)
notables' tents and the European couple, lower right (~75% x, 75% y)
bihar.why: Sonepur Mela is one of Bihar's great gatherings; painted by Sewak Ram, it says "Bihar" for the two-homes chapter.
bihar.concerns: Same V&A licence problem as the musicians (non-commercial, 768 px); only 2500 px wide. Detail is fine-grained rather than bold.

bihar.title: Part of the city of Patna, on the river Ganges
bihar.creator: Thomas Daniell (1749 to 1840)
bihar.licence_evidence: Wellcome Collection catalogue API: licence "pdm" (work zur9r5a2). Europeana lists the same image as CC BY 4.0 from Wellcome.
bihar.shows: Patna's tall riverfront mansions and ghats above the Ganga, with big country boats moored below and a canopied boat on the shore.
zoom_details: country boats with masts at the ghat, lower left (~20% x, 75% y)
riverside mansions with balconies, centre (~50% x, 45% y)
canopied boat on the bank, right (~75% x, 70% y)
bihar.why: Patna seen from the Ganga, the river at the heart of Bihari life (and of Chhath).
bihar.concerns: A British view; quiet and monochrome-leaning. Better as a second image than a lead.

bihar.title: Street in Patna
bihar.creator: Sir Charles D'Oyly (1781 to 1845)
bihar.source: Yale Center for British Art, via Google Arts & Culture and Wikimedia Commons
bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page PD-Art (PD-old-100-expired). YCBA also releases its public-domain images openly.
bihar.shows: A busy lane of Patna City at golden evening light: thatched and tiled roofs, domed pavilions, a palanquin and riders moving through the crowd, and a big tree leaning over the street.
zoom_details: domed pavilions above the rooftops, upper left (~35% x, 30% y)
crowd and palanquin in the lane, lower left (~20% x, 75% y)

bihar.concerns: Dark oil with a heavy varnish tone; figures are small and loose. British artist.

bihar.title: Mithila painting: Sita and her friends bring the wedding garland to Rama (photograph)

bihar.licence_evidence: Wikimedia Commons file page {{self|cc-zero}} by the uploader-photographer. The painting itself carries no licence.
bihar.shows: A procession of women in striped skirts and saris carrying a lotus, a bowl and a garland, led by Sita in green, approaching blue Rama and his brothers, who hold a great garland; the ground is filled with flowers.

woman holding up a bowl, centre-left (~42% x, 25% y)
bihar.why: The jaimala of Sita, Mithila's daughter: the archetypal Bihari wedding, painted in Madhubani style. The best story fit of anything found.
bihar.concerns: Fails the strict rule as it stands: a CC0 photograph of a recent painting by an unnamed (probably living) artist, so the artwork's own copyright is not cleared. The image is also a cropped detail. Use only after identifying the artist and getting permission, or commission a similar painting.

maharashtra.title: Mahajanaka Jataka, Ajanta Cave 1 left wall: the king of Mithila's court, ceremonial bath and departure (photographic panorama)
maharashtra.place: Ajanta Cave 1, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad) district, Maharashtra
maharashtra.medium: Mural painting on plaster; stitched digital photograph
maharashtra.creator: Anonymous Vakataka-period Buddhist painters; photograph by Anandajoti Bhikkhu (Flickr 'Photo Dharma from Sadao, Thailand')
maharashtra.source: Wikimedia Commons (from Flickr)
maharashtra.licence: CC BY 2.0 (photograph); mural itself public domain
maharashtra.licence_evidence: Commons file page licence: CC BY 2.0, Flickr-reviewed; required credit 'Photo Dharma from Sadao, Thailand' (Anandajoti Bhikkhu).
maharashtra.shows: The whole upper left wall of Cave 1, about 7 m of the Mahajanaka story, above a cell doorway. At far left, a crowned king rides out on a white elephant beneath a palace gateway. Centre-left is a crowded court: the queen seated among women with joined hands, a crowned king among attendants, and figures with round instruments at the bottom. The centre shows palace balconies. At right is a pillared pavilion where women bathe and anoint the crowned king. Crowds and riders fill the lower right.
zoom_details: Far left (x~12%, y~55%): crowned king on the white elephant at the palace gate
Centre-left (x~30%, y~30%): the queen (Sivali) among her women, hands joined; women with round cymbal/drum-like objects below (x~32%, y~70%)
Right (x~68%, y~35%): the ceremonial bath, with jewelled women pouring water over the crowned king
Lower right (x~85%, y~75%): crowd and riders in procession
maharashtra.why: Mahajanaka Jataka (Pali Jataka no. 539): Mahajanaka is king of Mithila in Videha (north Bihar / Janakpur region). A Bihar story painted by Buddhist artists in Maharashtra 1,500 years ago is the cleanest possible bridge between the two families and the two faiths. It works as the 'two homes' establishing image, or as the Shaadi panorama.
maharashtra.concerns: The story ends with Mahajanaka renouncing his throne and queen to become an ascetic; that is an odd moral for a wedding, so captions should stay on Mithila, the court and the bath rather than the plot. The mural is patchy, with grey losses, and a dark doorway sits in the lower centre. Most scholars (Schlingloff, MAP Academy) identify the wall as Mahajanaka; a minority read it as a Mahavastu version. CC BY 2.0 needs visible credit.

maharashtra.title: Lustration of the king (Mahajanaka's ceremonial bath), Ajanta Cave 1: Herringham 'Ajanta Frescoes' colour plate XIV
maharashtra.date: Mural c. 460-480 CE; copy made 1909-11; published 1915
maharashtra.place: Copied in Ajanta Cave 1 (left wall, between the cell doors), Maharashtra; printed in London
maharashtra.medium: Tempera/watercolour copy, reproduced as a colour plate (scanned at 300 ppi)
maharashtra.creator: Lady Christiana Herringham's copying team; the book's table of plates appears to credit Samarendranath Gupta (1887-1964) for plates XIV-XV
maharashtra.source: Internet Archive: Smithsonian Libraries copy of 'Ajanta Frescoes' (India Society, 1915)
maharashtra.licence_evidence: archive.org item ajantafrescoes00royaa (Smithsonian Libraries scan), metadata field possible-copyright-status: 'Public domain. The Library considers that this work is no longer under copyright protection.' Book published London, India Society, 1915.
maharashtra.shows: A crowned prince sits on a low stool in a palace hall with pearl festoons and vase-shaped roof finials. About twelve jewelled women in striped skirts surround him: one lifts a vessel to pour water over him, others hold a mirror, a fly-whisk, a pitcher and trays. A boy kneels at his feet by a basin, and a garden of rosettes is painted on the floor.
zoom_details: Centre (x~45%, y~50%): the crowned king, hands together, as the water is poured
Upper right (x~70%, y~40%): a woman raising a vessel and another adjusting her earring
Bottom centre (x~40%, y~85%): the boy at his feet with the water basin and pitcher stand
Top band (x~50%, y~12%): the palace cornice with vase finials and hanging pearl strings
maharashtra.why: Haldi is the pre-wedding anointing and bath, done by the women of the house. This is a royal anointing-bath from the same Mithila story as the Cave 1 wall, so the Haldi chapter continues the Bihar-Maharashtra thread. The 1910 copy is far clearer and brighter than the mural is today.
maharashtra.concerns: This is an early-20th-century copy, not a photograph of the mural; colours are idealised. Upper bodies are bare, as in the original. Copyright: the work is public domain in the US (published 1915) and in India (life+60 for Gupta expired 2025). In life+70 countries (UK/EU) a copyist's share could theoretically last to 2034, though a faithful copy of an ancient mural likely carries no new copyright. The OCR'd copyist list did not match a signature on another plate, so verify the credit. The IIIF crop URL returns about 2.7 MB.

maharashtra.title: King, queen and attendants in a palace pavilion (Mahajanaka cycle), Ajanta Cave 1: Herringham colour plate XV

maharashtra.medium: Tempera/watercolour copy reproduced as a colour plate

maharashtra.source: Internet Archive: Smithsonian Libraries copy of 'Ajanta Frescoes' (1915)

maharashtra.shows: A pillared pavilion with a sloping roof and pearl festoons. Inside, a king in a tall jewelled crown leans toward his queen while a woman behind lifts something to his lips. Women with joined hands and striped skirts stand at the right pillar. Two boys sit at the bottom by a footed bowl, and a garland-holding attendant leans in at left.
zoom_details: Centre-left (x~35%, y~45%): the crowned king, jewelled collar and armlets
Centre (x~52%, y~45%): the queen and the attendant offering him food or drink
Right (x~80%, y~45%): a woman with folded hands and a bangled arm at the pillar
Bottom (x~45%, y~88%): two boys beside the footed bowl
maharashtra.why: A royal couple seated together in a festooned pavilion: a natural 'mandap' image for the Shaadi. It belongs to the same Cave 1 Mithila story, so the whole site can stay inside one story.
maharashtra.concerns: Most likely Mahajanaka and Sivali (Herringham left it unidentified; its position next to the bath scene implies it). The copyright note is the same as for plate XIV. There is mild nudity typical of Ajanta. An alternative photograph of the mural is Commons 'Mahajanaka jataka Ajanta Cave 1.jpg' (CC BY-SA 4.0, 5198x3462), but it is dim.

maharashtra.title: Bodhisattva Padmapani (the lotus-bearer), Ajanta Cave 1
maharashtra.place: Ajanta Cave 1, back wall left of the shrine antechamber, Maharashtra

maharashtra.source: Wikimedia Commons (from Flickr)

maharashtra.shows: The famous over-life-size Bodhisattva with a tall jewelled crown, downcast eyes and a pearl necklace, holding a blue lotus in his right hand. A dark-skinned attendant princess is at lower right, with celestial musicians, monkeys and rocky-landscape figures in the upper corners.
zoom_details: Face and jewelled crown (x~45%, y~28%)
Right hand holding the blue lotus (x~45%, y~55%)
Dark-skinned attendant princess, lower right (x~78%, y~72%)
Upper left (x~15%, y~15%): heavenly musician (kinnara with veena) and onlookers
maharashtra.why: The single most iconic image of Maharashtra's Buddhist heritage: compassion holding a lotus. It is a gentle and respectful opening blessing from the bride's tradition, and it works as a cover.
maharashtra.concerns: The cave is dim and the photo has a warm yellow cast; the lower third has dark losses. CC BY 2.0 needs credit. Alternatives: Commons 'Padmapani Bodhisattva-Ajanta Caves-Aurangabad-Maharashtra.jpg' (CC BY-SA 4.0, 4000x6000) and the Herringham lotus-offering plate below.

maharashtra.title: Offering lotus-flowers to the Bodhisattva, Ajanta Cave 1: Herringham colour plate X

maharashtra.shows: A bodhisattva in an elaborate gold-and-jewel crown, pearl necklace with a blue pendant and striped lower garment, gesturing gracefully. At left, devotees climb toward him carrying lotus garlands and a tray heaped with white lotuses. Small crowned women watch from the bottom left, and a young woman with a jewelled hair ornament stands at the bottom right.
zoom_details: Jewelled crown and face (x~68%, y~25%)
Devotee with a tray piled with white lotuses (x~28%, y~58%)
Couple bringing offerings, top left (x~20%, y~20%)
Young woman with hair ornament, bottom right (x~85%, y~85%)
maharashtra.why: It shows people arriving with flowers to honour someone, an apt metaphor for guests arriving with blessings. It is cleaner and more legible than the dark Padmapani photo, and in the same Buddhist register.
maharashtra.concerns: This is a copy. Syad Ahmad's dates are unknown, but the work has been public domain in the US since its 1915 publication, and a faithful copy of an ancient mural carries little or no new authorship. Herringham queried the identification (Avalokitesvara?).

maharashtra.shows: A tall princess in a jewelled crown and girdle gazes into a hand mirror. A maid at right holds a tray with small cosmetic pots, another maid at left adjusts something, and a child kneels at lower right. Maid's tray with ointment and cosmetic pots (x~72%, y~42%)
Kneeling child at the feet (x~78%, y~75%)
Stepped plinth and jewelled anklets (x~50%, y~90%)
maharashtra.why: Adornment before a ceremony, with maidens bringing ointments: an exact visual rhyme for Haldi, where the bride is anointed by the women of her family.
maharashtra.concerns: The princess's upper body is bare (Ajanta convention), which may not suit every relative. The tall format needs a portrait or cropped pin.

maharashtra.shows: A prince and princess sit close on a cushioned couch in a coral-red pavilion with green-capped pillars. A dark-skinned maid holds a jug behind them, faces peer through a window at upper left, a seated attendant in white is at lower left, and a small figure crouches at their feet.

Maid with the water jug, right (x~75%, y~40%)
Faces at the window, upper left (x~18%, y~33%)
Seated attendant in white, lower left (x~18%, y~75%)
maharashtra.why: The most tender couple image at Ajanta, in a festive red pavilion: a good Shaadi close or 'together' moment.
maharashtra.concerns: The copy is by Nandalal Bose (d. 1966): public domain in the US (published 1915) and in India from 1 Jan 2027 (life+60), but in life+70 countries until the end of 2036, if a faithful copy is protectable at all. If that matters, use the CC BY-SA 4.0 photo 'Ajanta amorous palace scene.jpg' (Commons, 2995x2623) instead. The scene is intimate rather than ceremonial.

maharashtra.title: Two donor couples flanking the Buddha, verandah of the Great Chaitya, Karla (Karle) Caves
maharashtra.date: Couples c. 1st century CE; Buddha panel later (c. 5th-6th century); photograph 2017

maharashtra.source: Wikimedia Commons (from Flickr)

maharashtra.shows: Two life-size mithuna (donor) couples in heavy turbans, earrings and girdles stand arm in arm, one on each side. Between them, under a horseshoe arch, is a smaller panel of the Buddha teaching on a lotus throne with attendants, with tiny worshippers below.

maharashtra.shows: Under a row of scalloped arches with pointed pendants, the young bride, veiled and in a patterned sari, bows with joined hands before seated elders. The elders are women in red-and-yellow nine-yard saris and a crowned king holding a sword and shield. maharashtra.title: Phugadi (Fugdi): women's dance game, Chitrashala Press print no. 102

maharashtra.why: Fugdi and jhimma are the Marathi women's games played at Mangalagaur and pre-wedding gatherings. It is printed in Pune by Chitrashala, with Devanagari captions, which makes it the most Marathi Sangeet image possible.
maharashtra.concerns: Wellcome titles it 'A girl and boy dance'; the crowned right-hand figure may be Krishna or a woman in costume, so caption it as fugdi. There are some surface cracks. 2346 px wide is fine but not huge.

maharashtra.title: Gauri (गौरी)

maharashtra.shows: A bust-length Maharashtrian woman with a golden halo, jewelled crown, crescent-and-bindi forehead mark and a pearl nath (nose ring), with layered necklaces. zoom_details: Nath (pearl nose ring) and earrings (x~50%, y~45%)
Jewelled crown and halo (x~50%, y~18%)
Stacked necklaces (thushi/putali-style) (x~50%, y~65%)
Marathi caption 'गौरी' (x~50%, y~96%)
maharashtra.why: Gauri is worshipped by Marathi brides before the wedding (the Gauri-Har puja), and this print is the archetypal Marathi bridal look: nath, green choli, red sari. It was made near Pune.
maharashtra.concerns: It is a Hindu goddess. The bride's family is Buddhist, and Ambedkar's 1956 vows explicitly renounce worship of Gauri and Ganapati, so ask the couple. If used, it may fit better as 'Marathi adornment' than as devotion. Single-figure portrait with few distinct zoom points.

zoom_details: Ganesha's crown and peacock halo (x~50%, y~25%)

Attendants with chauris (x~15%, y~30%)

maharashtra.why: Marathi weddings conventionally open with Ganesha, and this is Ganesha as a married deity, printed near Pune. It suits the groom's Hindu side if the opening blessing is meant to be shared.
maharashtra.concerns: This is not Buddhist, and the 22 vows of Navayana Buddhism explicitly reject Ganapati worship. Treat it as groom's-side only and only with the couple's approval. Ravi Varma died in 1906; the print is public domain.

maharashtra.concerns: A Hindu epic scene; check with the bride's family. It is a print after Ravi Varma, not an original.

maharashtra.concerns: The holding institution is not named on Commons, only the Google Arts & Culture source; PD-Art applies regardless. It is a single figure with a plain background, so there are 3-4 good zoom points.

objects.why: Only usable openly licensed image found of the sindoor box (sinhora) at the heart of the Bihari sindoor-daan rite. Shallow depth of field gives natural zoom targets.
objects.concerns: Modern photo, not heritage; CC BY-SA requires attribution and share-alike for adapted versions. Box is a modern beaded/decorated one, not a traditional lacquered wooden sinhora. Bride is anonymous (face not shown).

objects.title: Tambura (front)
objects.medium: Gourd, wood, ivory, bone, paint, steel
objects.creator: Unknown

zoom_details: Saraswati with two peacocks at the top of the soundboard
Painted figures/musicians on the lower soundboard
Ivory inlay pattern running up the neck
The bridge and pegs
objects.why: An instrument explicitly from Maharashtra, with Saraswati (goddess of music) painted on it: a ready-made Sangeet invocation. Tall format suits a vertical scroll.
objects.concerns: Painted figures are small on the soundboard; zooms need the full-res file.

objects.title: Tambura (back of gourd)
objects.medium: Gourd, wood, ivory, bone, paint, steel
objects.creator: Unknown
objects.licence_evidence: Met Collection API isPublicDomain: true (additionalImages of object 500758).
objects.shows: The same tambura from behind: a turmeric-orange gourd painted all over with dancing figures among flowering trees, and gold-and-red floral medallions on the neck.
zoom_details: Dancing couple painted on the gourd
Gilt floral medallion on the neck
Black-and-gold petal collar where neck meets gourd
objects.why: Same object, warmer palette: an orange-yellow painted gourd full of dancers is almost a Sangeet poster, and doubles for Haldi colours.
objects.concerns: Shares an object with the front view - pick one per site or use both in one tour.

objects.title: Dancer with two musicians (sarangi and drum)
objects.creator: Unknown photographer
objects.licence: Public domain (photo c.1860-70); donated by KITLV, originally CC BY-SA 4.0
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page: {{KITLV donation}}, Leiden University Library handle http://hdl.handle.net/1887.1/item:818862; original GWToolset metadata permission CC-BY-SA-4.0 (OTRS 2015041410012461).
objects.shows: A dancer in a full skirt and veil spreads her skirt mid-step between a seated sarangi player and a drummer, in a pillared courtyard.
zoom_details: The dancer's swirling skirt and jewellery
Sarangi player on the left
Drummer with a barrel drum (dholak) on the right
objects.why: The earliest-looking, most cinematic image of music and dance found in this track; three clear subjects for a 3-step zoom.
objects.concerns: "Nautch" carried courtesan connotations in colonial captions; place unknown (probably north India, not specifically Bihar/Maharashtra). Licence statement on Commons is the KITLV donation template; worst case CC BY-SA 4.0 (still allowed).

objects.title: Sitar
objects.medium: Gourd and wood with pigment, ivory and bone; copper-alloy frets; iron strings
objects.creator: Unknown
objects.licence_evidence: Cleveland Open Access API share_license_status = "CC0".
objects.shows: A red-lacquered sitar with gold painted floral panels on neck and gourd, curved metal frets and tuning pegs.
zoom_details: Gold floral panel at the top of the neck
Row of curved frets
Painted gourd with bone bridge
objects.why: Best openly licensed instrument from eastern India (Bihar was administered as part of Bengal in 1850); red and gold suits the Shaadi palette.
objects.concerns: Labelled Bengal/Bangladesh, not Bihar. Diagonal studio shot with a scale bar at the bottom. No Bihar-specific instrument found.

objects.title: Curcuma longa L. (turmeric), plate 178
objects.creator: Franz Eugen Köhler (ed.), Köhler's Medizinal-Pflanzen; drawings by Walther Müller / C. F. Schmidt
objects.source: Biodiversity Heritage Library (Missouri Botanical Garden copy)

objects.shows: A turmeric plant: one huge curving leaf, a pale green-and-white flower spike with orange-yellow flowers, dissected flower parts, and a line drawing of the rhizome with roots.
zoom_details: The flower spike with orange flowers
The knobbly rhizome (the haldi itself) with its roots
A single orange flower in section
The sweeping leaf
objects.why: The classic, crisp turmeric plate: strong graphic layout, yellow-orange accents, and the root that becomes haldi paste.
objects.concerns: German publication, not Indian. BHL site is behind a bot wall; the S3 open-data URL works. Commons copy is only 1438x1969.

objects.title: Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.): rhizome with flowering stem and separate leaf and floral segments
objects.creator: After Franz Anton von Scheidl (for N. J. Jacquin)
objects.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome); CC BY 4.0 on Commons copy
objects.licence_evidence: Wellcome Catalogue API location licence id "pdm" for V0042925; Commons copy tagged CC BY 4.0 (older Wellcome release).
objects.shows: A tall plate: white flower spike, papery sheathing leaf stalks and a great cluster of rhizomes at the base, some cut open to show their orange flesh.
zoom_details: Cut rhizome showing bright orange interior
Cluster of finger-like rhizomes and roots
White flower spike at top
objects.why: The best image of the actual haldi root: the cut orange flesh is a perfect close-up for the Haldi chapter.
objects.concerns: Narrow format and only 1181 px wide (3109 tall) - below ideal; good for a vertical scroll only.

objects.title: Curcuma montana (a wild turmeric), plate 151
objects.place: Drawn in India (Coromandel coast); published London
objects.medium: Hand-coloured engraving after an Indian artist's drawing
objects.creator: William Roxburgh, Plants of the Coast of Coromandel vol. 2, t. 151
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page: {{PD-old-70-expired}} (published 1798).
objects.shows: A whole turmeric-family plant with broad ribbed leaves, a white-and-pink flower spike, and rhizome with spidery roots.
zoom_details: White and pink flower bracts
Rhizome and roots
Flower dissection drawn at left
objects.why: Huge, elegant, and made from drawings by Indian artists for Roxburgh - an Indian-made counterpart to the Köhler plate.
objects.concerns: This is Curcuma montana, a wild relative, not the culinary/ritual turmeric (C. longa). The rhizome is pale, not orange.

objects.title: East Indian Lotus (Nelumbo nucifera)
objects.place: India (Company school; NGA attributes to "British 19th Century")
objects.creator: Unknown (attributed "British 19th Century")
objects.source: National Gallery of Art, Washington, 1970.19.1 (Ailsa Mellon Bruce Collection)
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file (donated by NGA under its Open Access policy): permission {{CC0}}; NGA open-access images are CC0.
objects.shows: A white lotus in full bloom above two large blue-green leaves, with a closed bud and a rolled young leaf, on warm buff paper.
zoom_details: The open flower with its green seed-pod centre
The closed bud
Veins radiating across a lotus leaf
The rolled young leaf
objects.why: The lotus is sacred to both families (Buddha's seat; Lakshmi; Kohbar). Calm, luminous, high-res, with lots of negative space for text.
objects.concerns: NGA labels it "British 19th Century" though it looks like Company-school work; this is a painting, so check for overlap with the paintings track.

objects.title: Nelumbium speciosum (sacred lotus), from Illustrations of Indian Botany vol. 1
objects.place: Madras (published by J. B. Pharoah for the author)
objects.creator: Robert Wight (drawings by Indian artist Rungiah)
objects.source: Wikimedia Commons from Internet Archive b21913109_0001 (Wellcome Library copy)
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page: Book template, published 1840, PD (no rights holder); source Internet Archive b21913109_0001.
objects.shows: A white lotus, petals drawn in fine hatched lines, set against a huge green lotus leaf whose veins radiate from a pale centre.
zoom_details: Golden seed-pod and stamens at the heart of the flower
Radiating veins from the leaf centre
The prickly stalk
objects.why: Indian-published, graphic and bold - the leaf-as-mandala works beautifully as a full-bleed background.
objects.concerns: Page crop from a scanned book: slight paper tone/bleed; artist credit (Rungiah) is my inference from Wight's practice, not stated on the file.

objects.title: Peepal tree, bodhi tree or bo tree (inscribed "Ficus religiosa Linn ... Bar Tree", No. 83)
objects.creator: Unknown Indian artist
objects.source: Royal Albert Memorial Museum & Art Gallery, Exeter, 19/1927/2/83 (Richard Cresswell collection)
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page: permission {{PD-old-70}}, licence header {{CC0}}; institution RAMM.
objects.shows: A single great tree with a massive trunk and rounded clouds of finely drawn leaves, on a strip of ground with small plants; ink inscriptions along the bottom.
zoom_details: Finely drawn leaf clusters of the canopy
The twisting trunk and roots
Handwritten label "Ficus religiosa" and "No 83"
objects.why: The Bodhi tree of Bodh Gaya (Bihar) painted by an Indian artist: sacred to the Buddhist bride and Hindu groom alike - the "two homes under one tree" image.
objects.concerns: Label also says "Bar Tree" (bar = banyan) - possible mis-identification by the original collector. Only 1554 px wide. It is a painting (check overlap with paintings track).

objects.title: Peepul tree (Ficus religiosa): fruiting stem
objects.creator: After M. A. Burnett (Plantae utiliores)
objects.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome); CC BY 4.0 on Commons copy
objects.licence_evidence: Wellcome Catalogue API licence id "pdm" for V0043954.
objects.shows: One large heart-shaped peepal leaf with its long drip tip, smaller leaves, and three dark purple figs, with "Ficus religiosa" in copperplate.
zoom_details: The drip-tip of the heart-shaped leaf
The cluster of purple figs
The copperplate inscription "Ficus religiosa"
objects.why: The peepal leaf is the most recognisable Buddhist/Bodh Gaya symbol; simple and iconic, ideal for an opening blessing or a closing card.
objects.concerns: European lithograph; plain composition gives only 2-3 zooms.

objects.title: Mango (Mangifera indica): branch with flowers, fruit and leaves
objects.creator: Hendrik van Rheede, Hortus Malabaricus
objects.licence: Public Domain Mark (Wellcome); CC BY 4.0 on Commons copy
objects.licence_evidence: Wellcome Catalogue API licence id "pdm" for V0042598.
objects.shows: A spreading mango branch with long glossy leaves, flower panicles and hanging fruit, a cut fruit, and names in Latin, Malayalam, Devanagari ("Ambo") and Arabic.
zoom_details: A spray of long mango leaves (the toran leaf)
Flower panicle
Name label in four scripts incl. Devanagari "Ambo"
objects.why: Mango leaves hang in the toran at both a Bihari and a Marathi door; the Devanagari "Ambo" echoes Marathi "amba". Lots of leaves to zoom across.
objects.concerns: Hand-colourist painted the fruit purple-blue, which looks odd; crop to leaves. A whole-tree plate (V0042597) also exists.

objects.title: Caryophyllus Indicus (African/Indian marigold, Tagetes), Classis Aestiva fol. 172
objects.creator: Basilius Besler, Hortus Eystettensis
objects.source: Biodiversity Heritage Library (Missouri Botanical Garden copy), via Wikimedia Commons

zoom_details: A double marigold head in close-up
Single marigold flower
Engraved Latin caption "Caryophyllus Indicus..."
objects.why: Marigold garlands are the visual signature of both weddings; Besler's pom-poms are dramatic and could be tinted saffron by the designer.
objects.concerns: Black and white (the hand-coloured 1613 copies online are low-res). European plate; the name "Indicus" is historical, not Indian origin.

objects.title: Parvati Temple and Hill, seen from the Parvati Lake at Poona
objects.creator: Unknown photographer
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page permission: {{PD-old-70-1923}} {{KITLV donation}}.

zoom_details: Parvati temple on the hilltop
The two figures on the bank looking out
Reflections and the old embankment wall across the lake
objects.why: Pune's best-known skyline in a tranquil 1870s view - the bride's home city as it was 150 years ago. Huge file, sepia, very cinematic.
objects.concerns: Sepia/low contrast; temple is small in the frame (zoom needs the full TIFF).

objects.title: Mahabodhi temple, Bodh Gaya, before restoration
objects.medium: Photograph (album "The Ancient Monuments, Temples and Sculptures of India", part II)
objects.creator: Unknown (probably J. D. Beglar / Archaeological Survey)
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page permission: {{PD-old-70-1923}} {{KITLV donation}}.
objects.shows: The great brick spire of the Mahabodhi temple, crumbling and overgrown, with palms and shrubs at its foot, before the 1880s restoration.
zoom_details: The broken finial at the top
Rows of niches on the tower
Arched doorway and window at the base
Palms beside the temple
objects.why: The temple at the place of the Buddha's enlightenment, in Bihar - joins the Buddhist and Bihari threads in one image. Tall format suits a vertical tour.
objects.concerns: Shows the temple in ruin (some may find it melancholy for a wedding). Date/author uncertain. A c.1915 view of the restored temple (KITLV 1405912) exists but is small on its mount.

objects.title: Groom on horseback
objects.creator: William Johnson (Bombay photographer)
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page permission: {{PD-old-100-1923}} {{KITLV donation}}.
objects.shows: A young bridegroom in a tall headdress and brocade jama on a white horse hung with flower garlands, under a ceremonial parasol, with attendants holding round sun-fans.
zoom_details: The groom's headdress and face
Flower garlands hanging from the horse
Embroidered parasol overhead
Attendant with a round ceremonial fan
objects.why: A real 1850s baraat moment - the groom arriving on a garlanded horse - one of the earliest wedding photographs from Maharashtra. Superb detail at 5859 px.
objects.concerns: The groom appears to be a child (child marriage was common then) - caption with care. Community not recorded (Johnson photographed many Gujarati/Parsi Bombay sitters).

objects.title: The bride's mother applying haldi to her (Jharkhand)
objects.creator: Disha Shinde 08 (Wikimedia Commons user)
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page: {{self|cc-by-sa-4.0}}, own work.
objects.shows: Warm low light: a mother's hand with red-and-white bangles smoothing turmeric onto her daughter's forehead; the bride, eyes closed, in a yellow polka-dot sari.
zoom_details: Turmeric on the bride's forehead
Red and white bangles on the mother's wrist
Yellow sari with red dots
objects.why: An intimate, golden Haldi moment from Jharkhand - the groom's home state now (Ranchi). Emotional and on-palette.
objects.concerns: Identifiable private individuals; consider privacy/personality rights before featuring a stranger's face on a personal wedding site. Modern photo; CC BY-SA needs attribution.

objects.title: Raw turmeric paste for haldi ceremony in Indian wedding
objects.creator: Debapriya Manna (Wikimedia Commons user)

zoom_details: Mound of turmeric paste in the brass bowl
White rice-paste floor drawing
Brass lota with its rim
objects.why: A no-faces still life of the Haldi itself; high-res and colourful, safe to use without privacy worries.
objects.concerns: Modern photo, likely a Bengali wedding (alpana), not Bihari/Marathi specifically. CC BY-SA attribution needed.

objects.title: Hindoostan (map of India)
objects.creator: James Rennell; engraved by J. Phillips and W. Harrison
objects.source: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division, G7625 1782 .R4
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page: {{LOC-map}} (Library of Congress, no known restrictions; published 1782).

zoom_details: Patna and Bahar on the Ganges
Poona in the Maratha Deccan
The route between them across central India
Decorative title roundel (optional)
objects.why: One sheet that holds both homes 1,600 km apart; enormous resolution lets the camera fly from Patna to Poona.
objects.concerns: The cartouche shows Brahmins handing scriptures to Britannia (colonial allegory) - avoid zooming on it. Fold seam across the middle.

objects.title: A New Map of Hindoostan, from the Latest Authorities

Poonah in the Deccan
Oval title cartouche
Handwritten 1823 margin note

objects.title: Votive Plaque with Figure of the Buddha, Temple at Bodhgaya, and Stupas

Temple spire above with flame-like ornament
Rows of miniature stupas
The inscription band

objects.concerns: Small object (15 cm); sculpture rather than painting but may overlap with another track's Buddhist material.

objects.title: Votive Model of the Mahabodhi Temple, Bodh Gaya
objects.creator: Unknown
objects.licence_evidence: Commons file page licence {{PD-LACMA}}; LACMA object page publicDomain:1.

The open sanctum doorway
Stepped tower top
